passage: Thursday. Day four with the new library and I have nothing working. My decision is that the documentation is the only honest source: no videos, no forum answers, no examples from strangers. Bhupen said, "Just watch one ten-minute video." I said no. So I read page after page of the official docs. Problem: they assume I already know three other things: what a build tool is, what a package registry is, and what a "module" means here. Every sentence sends me to another page. I lost three days going in circles. Bhupen watched me and did not say a word, which is worse. I am tired and my pride is not helping. Tomorrow: one video, and a real example. — Rajni

passage:
The power had gone again in the lanes of the small town, so Damini sat in the cyber café running on the inverter, a new online form tool open on screen. Her uncle's milk cooperative wanted its collection records moved online, and Damini, the only one in the family studying computers, had promised to do it in a week.
It was now day five. She had read the official manual twice, all sixty pages, and still did not understand what a 'schema' was; the manual used the word on page one as if everyone knew. Nandini, who ran the café, pointed to a short local-language video playing on the next screen for another customer. 'Ten minutes, didi. It shows the whole thing.'
'Videos make people lazy,' Damini said, and turned back to page thirty-one.
On day seven the cooperative secretary came by. There was nothing to show.

qa.q: How many pages was the official manual?
Why did Damini turn back to page thirty-one, and what was she likely feeling?
qa.a: She felt stubborn and proud about doing it the proper way, and perhaps anxious about the week's promise, so she dismissed the video as making people lazy.

qa.q: Which approach would suit Damini better on day five?
qa.a: Watching the short video for the big picture, then using the manual for details like the schema, would likely have saved days.

qa.q: How might the cooperative secretary see day seven?
qa.a: The secretary likely feels let down, since a week was promised and there was nothing to show.

grounding: Shows a student in a small town insisting on the official manual alone and losing a week because it assumes knowledge the student lacks.
